deflator: CPIAUCSL (BLS CPI-U All Urban Consumers; annual mean of monthly NSA index)

primary.healthcare_definition: Full KFF average annual family premium (employer + employee share)
primary.rationale: Incidence theory: employer-paid premiums suppress wages, so the full premium is a real cost the household bears.

lower_bound.rationale: Cash-flow conservative measure: only what the household directly pays out of pocket. Skeptic-proof lower bound.

dream_index_variants.crossing_year_definition: First year the index exceeds 1.0 (annual median household income).

housing.method: Annual mortgage payment on real 2024 home price; 20% down, 80% financed, 30-year fixed amortization
notes: MSPUS held in real-2024 terms at 1963 value for 1960-1962. Spec called for Case-Shiller (CSUSHPISA) extrapolation, but CSUSHPISA does not begin until 1987.
Mortgage rate held at the 1971 annual mean for 1960-1970 (MORTGAGE30US starts 1971).

primary.anchor_source: KFF 2024 Employer Health Benefits Survey, average annual total family premium
primary.rationale: Per economic incidence theory, employer-paid premiums are a cost the household ultimately bears (suppressed wages). Used as the primary 'cost of middle-class healthcare' figure.

lower_bound.anchor_source: KFF 2024 Employer Health Benefits Survey: employee premium share + average deductible
lower_bound.rationale: Conservative cash-flow measure capturing only what the household directly pays. Excludes employer-paid premiums.

healthcare.notes: Will be replaced with direct KFF survey microdata in a later step.

education.deflator: CPIEDUSL (BLS Education CPI, 1993+); CPIAUCSL fallback for pre-1993
education.method: anchor * CPIEDUSL[y] / CPIEDUSL[2024], with CPIAUCSL fallback before 1993

childcare.anchor_source: ChildCare Aware of America 2024 national median (center-based infant care)
childcare.deflator: CUSR0000SEEB (BLS CPI Tuition, Other School Fees, and Childcare); CPIAUCSL fallback for pre-1978
childcare.deviation_from_spec: Spec named CUSR0000SEEB03; that series ID does not exist on FRED. Substituted CUSR0000SEEB ('Tuition, Other School Fees, and Childcare'), the closest available BLS series. Bundles tuition with childcare.

transportation.anchor_source: AAA 2024 Your Driving Costs, average annual new-vehicle ownership and operating cost

food.anchor_source: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2023 average food expenditure, inflated to 2024 with food CPI

income.primary_method: Approach B: MEHOINUSA646N (nominal) * (CPI_2024/CPI_y) via CPIAUCSL annual means
income.spec_deviation: Spec says 'Use dream_index_A as the final value', but A and B do not agree because Census's real series (MEHOINUSA672N) uses CPI-U-RS while the project's CORE mandate requires CPI-U (CPIAUCSL). Choosing B preserves internal consistency with every other component, which all use CPI-U.
income.approach_A_series: MEHOINUSA672N (real, chained 2024 USD per latest Census rebase; implicit deflator = CPI-U-RS)
income.pre_1984_extension: Years 1960-1983: extended using MEFAINUSA672N (median family income, chained 2024 USD) rescaled by the 1984 household/family ratio = 0.8480. Inherits Census's CPI-U-RS deflation (minor inconsistency relative to CPI-U used elsewhere).
income.FRED_rebase_note: Spec described MEHOINUSA672N as 'chained 2017 dollars'; FRED has since rebased it to chained 2024 dollars (verified: 672N[2024] == 646N[2024] = 83,730). No CPI_2024/CPI_2017 rescaling applied.

integrity_check.comparison: dream_index_A (Census's real income, CPI-U-RS basis) vs dream_index_B (CPI-U-deflated nominal)
integrity_check.interpretation: A failure here indicates Census's CPI-U-RS and our CPI-U deflators diverge for older years. This is a known, expected divergence; CPI-U-RS retroactively applies modern BLS methods to pre-1999 indexes, lowering measured inflation. Project chose CPI-U (Approach B) for cross-component consistency.
